voices.note: the mishna clause on the thigh bone of a carcass and of a creeping animal, cited as lemma at 126b.5

props.gloss_en: the mishna's clause on the thigh bone of a carcass and the thigh bone of a creeping animal, cited by its opening words
the baraita: 'benivlatah' (one who touches its carcass) -- and not [one who touches] a sealed thigh bone
the baraita: one might think even if it was perforated; the verse says 'one who touches ... shall be impure' -- what can be touched is impure, and what cannot be touched is pure
Abaye: go out and see how many orifices there are in it [the animal]
Rava: come and see how many threads extend from it [the kidney]
Rav Oshaya's dilemma, first side: [a thigh bone] he intended to perforate and did not -- lacking perforation is like lacking an act
Rav Oshaya then resolved it: lacking perforation is not like lacking an act
